text:
sofia: quick q — thinking through per-route "grace window" for quotas. if a route allows short bursts but the acct-level quota is exhausted, what's our preferred 429 contract? do we rely on Retry-After only for backcompat, or add new X-RateLimit-* headers? :thinking:

raj: I vote: keep Retry-After for old clients, but emit X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset for newer SDKs. older SDKs ignore extra headers so should be ok.

morgan: also: how do we signal that the 429 came from a route soft-limit vs account hard-limit? clients might want different UX.

ana: we (ana) could add a small machine-readable code in the body e.g. {"error":"quota_exceeded","scope":"route","policy":"grace"} — human-friendly msg for old clients still works.

sofia: yea machine code + Retry-After seems safest. but worried about mobile SDKs that only look for Retry-After and then retry aggressively — grace window is supposed to be short (100ms-2s) and *not* retried by clients. how do we prevent retry storms?

raj: option: use short Retry-After for grace (e.g. 1s) but include header X-Backoff-Suggest: "no-retry" for new SDKs. or X-RateLimit-Reset with epoch to indicate exact unlock. old SDKs will still wait Retry-After, new ones follow reset.

morgan: +1 to explicit bucket id too. if we provide X-RateLimit-Bucket, proxies can aggregate. header samples: ```
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1615000000
X-RateLimit-Bucket: route:chat-completions:v2
X-Quota-Policy: grace
```

jake: a couple implementation checks: 1) ensure Dedicated mode respects customer-level commit and doesn't surface grace windows that bypass reserved capacity. 2) Private deploys may want opt-out header to minimize header churn.

ana: for backcompat, I think we should: (a) always send Retry-After when we return 429, (b) add X-RateLimit-* headers if we know the bucket, (c) include small error.code in body. that covers mobile and web.

sofia: sounds good. can we agree on exact header names and semantics? propose: X-RateLimit-Limit (int), X-RateLimit-Remaining (int), X-RateLimit-Reset (unix secs), X-RateLimit-Bucket (string), X-Quota-Policy (enum: hard|grace|burst), X-Backoff-Suggest (enum: retry|no-retry) and continue to set Retry-After (secs) always.

raj: fine but prefer X-Quota-Policy values: hard|soft|grace to avoid confusion. and X-Backoff-Suggest could be freeform but documented values are better.

morgan: ok let's lock names: X-RateLimit-*, X-Quota-Policy: hard|soft|grace, X-Backoff-Suggest: retry|no-retry. update sdk parsing docs to prefer X-Backoff-Suggest > X-RateLimit-Reset > Retry-After.

jake: can someone add a short config example for runtime? e.g. route config with burst, grace-window, bucket-id. I'll use it in the Dedicated onboarding playbook.

ana: here you go: ```yaml
routes:
  - id: chat-completions
    bucket: route:chat-completions:v2
    quotas:
      account: {period: 60, limit: 1000}
      route: {period: 1, burst: 100, grace_window_ms: 1500}
    policy: \"grace\"
```

sofia: perfect. last thing: telemetry/eventing. we should emit an event type quota.exhausted with fields: scope, bucket, policy, skipped_requests to console/metrics so product can monitor UX regressions.

raj: agree. also add a rollout note: start with grace-window disabled for Private until we ship opt-out flag. feature flag: feature.quota_grace_window.

morgan: i'll write the API contract PR and include sample responses + compat notes. tagging @jake for Dedicated checks. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: new PR created by morgan: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/4125 - includes headers, body codes, and runtime config.

jake: will review later today. thanks all. :rocket:
